title: Closing the water loop beyond 98 percent recovery
bottleneck: The ISS recycles about 98 percent of its water — but the remaining 2 percent loss, from brine, humidity, and unrecoverable waste streams, means a Mars crew would still need tons of resupply water over a multi-year mission. Brine dewatering, urine processing without consumable-heavy chemistry, and recovering water from solid waste all hit diminishing returns where each extra percent costs disproportionate mass, power, and complexity. True closure — zero net water loss — has never been demonstrated.
why_it_blocks: Water is the heaviest life-support consumable; without near-total recycling, Mars missions must land thousands of kilograms of water or bet everything on local ice mining working perfectly on the first try.
current_state: The ISS Water Recovery System approaches 98 percent with its brine processor; NASA's ECLSS roadmap targets higher closure for Mars. Fully closed multi-year operation has never been tested.
